title: The workspace ledger refreshes on branch/worktree change and on a ledger read — never per commit, and never from a process that outlives its trigger
context: Two refresh triggers were wrong on Windows for the same reason: a background child that outlives what started it keeps the repository directory open, so a test that deletes its clone right after fails with EBUSY (run 35190856782 job 105102951835, and the runner's cleanup log naming orphan node+git processes). A detached child at MCP session start was one; the post-commit hook backgrounding `workspaces snapshot` was the other, and worse — commits run right up to a test's teardown, and the snapshot's git work (up to a patch-id walk over the default branch) would be paid on the most frequent operation a developer performs.
decision: Refresh happens exactly where the ledger can actually change or is actually wanted: (1) the post-checkout hook, for branch checkouts only ($3 = 1), which is when branches and worktrees change; (2) `hunch worktree`, which creates one; (3) the `hunch_workspaces` MCP read, which publishes the observation it just took in the server process, reusing that snapshot via the pure `withPublishMode`; (4) `hunch workspaces snapshot` explicitly. The post-commit hook deliberately carries NO snapshot, and no trigger spawns a process that can outlive it. `HUNCH_WORKSPACE_REFRESH=0` makes the MCP read read-only.
consequences: `git commit` pays nothing for the ledger; only checkouts and explicit reads do.
A record can lag between a commit and the next checkout or ledger read; the freshness label ('unverified' past stale_after_days) is what keeps that honest.
No trigger leaves a child holding a repository directory, so a harness that deletes a clone immediately after its last commit is safe.
alternatives_rejected: Snapshot in the post-commit hook, backgrounded — a child alive at teardown held a Windows clone open (EBUSY) and taxed every commit with git work.
Snapshot in the post-commit hook, foreground — removes the orphan but makes every commit wait on a full snapshot, including a possible patch-id walk.
Detached child at MCP session start — the original orphan-process cause.
In-process timer at MCP session start — still races the server's own death mid-git on Windows, and writes into any MCP test running past the delay.
Retrying rmSync in the test's teardown — treats the symptom in the harness and leaves every real caller with a child that outlives its trigger.
